Ocean physics¶

Summary¶

This module holds the building-block physics for how the sea reflects and scatters a GNSS signal. It is a set of pure functions – no state, no classes – shared by the ocean target model. They answer four questions:

  • How well does seawater reflect at L-band? (its electrical properties, the permittivity)

  • How much of a flat surface bounces back? (the Fresnel and circular-polarisation reflectivities)

  • How rough is the sea? (the Cox-Munk wave-slope statistics and the Elfouhaily wave spectrum)

  • How much signal scatters back at an angle? (the Bragg and two-scale backscatter)

The implementation follows the cited published models. The tests pin algebraic identities, limiting cases, regression values and broad trends; they do not constitute independent validation against raw measurements or a mission-calibrated GNSS-R product.

Detailed Module Description¶

Seawater permittivity (Klein-Swift)¶

Permittivity says how strongly seawater responds to the radio wave; it sets how much of the signal reflects. The Klein-Swift model gives it as a Debye relaxation plus an ionic (salt) loss term,

(8)¶\[\varepsilon_r = \varepsilon_\infty + \frac{\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_\infty}{1 + j\,\omega\tau} - \frac{j\,\sigma_\mathrm{ion}}{\omega\,\varepsilon_0},\]

where \(\varepsilon_s\) is the low-frequency value, \(\varepsilon_\infty = 4.9\) the high-frequency limit, \(\tau\) the relaxation time, \(\sigma_\mathrm{ion}\) the salt conductivity, and \(\omega = 2\pi f\). The static value, relaxation time, and conductivity all depend on temperature and salinity (the polynomial fits in the code).

Fresnel and circular reflectivities¶

For a flat surface, the Fresnel coefficients give the reflection for the two linear polarisations, vertical (V) and horizontal (H):

(9)¶\[R_h = \frac{\cos\left(\theta\right) - \sqrt{\varepsilon_r - \sin^2\left(\theta\right)}}{\cos\left(\theta\right) + \sqrt{\varepsilon_r - \sin^2\left(\theta\right)}}, \qquad R_v = \frac{\varepsilon_r\cos\left(\theta\right) - \sqrt{\varepsilon_r - \sin^2\left(\theta\right)}}{\varepsilon_r\cos\left(\theta\right) + \sqrt{\varepsilon_r - \sin^2\left(\theta\right)}}.\]

GNSS transmits Right-Hand Circular (RHCP); a bounce flips most of it to Left-Hand (LHCP). Combining the Fresnel terms gives the circular reflectivities, cross-pol (the wanted RHCP->LHCP) and co-pol (RHCP->RHCP):

(10)¶\[R_\mathrm{RL} = \tfrac{1}{2}(R_h - R_v), \qquad R_\mathrm{RR} = \tfrac{1}{2}(R_h + R_v),\]

and the power reflectivities are \(|R_\mathrm{RL}|^2\) and \(|R_\mathrm{RR}|^2\).

How rough the sea is (Cox-Munk and Elfouhaily)¶

A rough sea has tilted facets. Cox-Munk give the spread of those tilts (the slope variance) as a simple function of wind speed, larger upwind than crosswind:

(11)¶\[\sigma_u^2 = 3.16\times 10^{-3}\,U_{10}, \qquad \sigma_c^2 = 3.0\times 10^{-3} + 1.92\times 10^{-3}\,U_{10},\]

and the chance of a given slope \((s_u, s_c)\) is a 2-D Gaussian,

(12)¶\[p(s_u, s_c) = \frac{1}{2\pi\,\sigma_u\,\sigma_c}\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{s_u^2}{2\sigma_u^2} - \frac{s_c^2}{2\sigma_c^2}\right).\]

For backscatter we need the wave height at one exact ripple size, not the whole-sea average. The Elfouhaily spectrum provides that. It is written as a curvature spectrum \(B(k)\) (a long-wave plus a short-wave part), and the height spectrum is

(13)¶\[S(k) = \frac{B(k)}{k^3} = \frac{B_\mathrm{low}(k) + B_\mathrm{high}(k)}{k^3}.\]

Bragg backscatter¶

Away from the specular direction (beyond ~20 deg), the return is dominated by Bragg scattering: the radar resonates with the one ripple whose spacing matches the wave, at wavenumber

(14)¶\[k_B = 2k\sin\left(\theta\right), \qquad k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}.\]

The first-order (small-ripple) backscatter cross-section per unit area is

(15)¶\[\sigma^0_{pp} = 8\pi\,k^4\cos^4\left(\theta\right)\,|g_{pp}|^2\,W_\mathrm{iso}(k_B),\]

where \(W_\mathrm{iso}(K) = S(K)/(2\pi K)\) is the roughness at the Bragg wavenumber and \(g_{pp}\) are the Bragg amplitudes for H and V. The circular amplitudes come from those:

(16)¶\[g_\mathrm{RL} = \tfrac{1}{2}(g_{HH} + g_{VV}), \qquad g_\mathrm{RR} = \tfrac{1}{2}(g_{HH} - g_{VV}).\]

Near nadir \(k_B \to 0\), the Bragg return vanishes and the quasi-specular (geometric-optics) term takes over, so this returns 0 there.

Two-scale (tilt) modulation¶

Real waves are small ripples riding on big swells. The big swells tilt the patches that carry the ripples, which changes the local angle the radar sees. The two-scale model averages the Bragg return over the spread of those tilts: for each facet slope it works out the local incidence angle, evaluates the Bragg return there, and averages with the slope probability. This lifts the return a couple of dB at low incidence and adds an upwind-vs-crosswind difference that first-order Bragg alone misses. The complete anisotropic slope covariance is rotated into the look/cross-look frame; its off-diagonal covariance is retained for intermediate wind-relative azimuths. As the swell slope goes to zero it reduces back to plain Bragg.

API reference¶

Pure-function helpers for ocean surface bistatic scattering physics.

Includes:

  • Seawater complex permittivity (Klein and Swift, 1977).

  • Fresnel reflection coefficients for vertical / horizontal polarisation.

  • Circular-polarisation power reflectivities (RHCP -> LHCP cross-pol, RHCP -> RHCP co-pol).

  • Cox-Munk (1954) clean-sea slope variances and 2-D Gaussian slope PDF.

All functions accept numpy scalars or arrays and broadcast accordingly.

functions.ocean_physics.seawater_permittivity(frequency_hz, temperature_c, salinity_psu)[source]¶

Complex relative permittivity of seawater (Klein and Swift, 1977).

The imaginary part is negative under the exp(+j omega t) convention used here (both Debye relaxation and ionic conductivity are losses, on the same negative-imaginary sign).

Parameters:

  • frequency_hz (scalar or array) – Carrier frequency [Hz].

  • temperature_c (scalar) – Sea temperature [degC] (valid range about -2 to 30).

  • salinity_psu (scalar) – Salinity [PSU] (valid range about 0 to 40).

Returns:

Relative permittivity (real minus j*imag).

Return type:

complex

functions.ocean_physics.fresnel_coefficients(theta_inc_rad, eps_r)[source]¶

Fresnel reflection coefficients for vertical (TM) and horizontal (TE) polarisation.

Parameters:

  • theta_inc_rad (scalar or array) – Incidence angle from the surface normal [rad].

  • eps_r (complex) – Relative permittivity of the lower medium (seawater).

Returns:

(R_v, R_h) complex Fresnel coefficients for vertical and horizontal polarisation.

Return type:

tuple

functions.ocean_physics.circular_pol_reflectivities(theta_inc_rad, eps_r)[source]¶

Power reflectivities for circular polarisation at the sea surface.

Uses the Fresnel sign convention R_v(0) = -R_h(0) (Ulaby, Moore and Fung 1982), so the cross-pol amplitude is R_RL = 0.5*(R_h - R_v) (RHCP to LHCP, dominant at low incidence) and the co-pol amplitude is R_RR = 0.5*(R_h + R_v) (RHCP to RHCP, grows toward grazing).

Parameters:

  • theta_inc_rad (scalar or array) – Incidence angle from the surface normal [rad].

  • eps_r (complex) – Relative permittivity of seawater.

Returns:

(R_RL_sq, R_RR_sq) power reflectivities (the squared magnitudes).

Return type:

tuple

functions.ocean_physics.cox_munk_slope_variances(wind_speed_m_s)[source]¶

Cox-Munk (1954) clean-sea slope variances at 10 m wind speed.

Parameters:

wind_speed_m_s (scalar) – Wind speed at 10 m [m/s].

Returns:

(sigma_u_sq, sigma_c_sq) upwind and crosswind slope variances [dimensionless].

Return type:

tuple

functions.ocean_physics.cox_munk_slope_pdf(s_u, s_c, sigma_u_sq, sigma_c_sq)[source]¶

2-D anisotropic Gaussian slope PDF in the wind-aligned (upwind, crosswind) frame.

Parameters:

  • s_u (scalar or array) – Slope components along the upwind / crosswind axes.

  • s_c (scalar or array) – Slope components along the upwind / crosswind axes.

  • sigma_u_sq (scalar) – Slope variances from cox_munk_slope_variances().

  • sigma_c_sq (scalar) – Slope variances from cox_munk_slope_variances().

Returns:

Probability density at the given slope.

Return type:

scalar or array

functions.ocean_physics.elfouhaily_omnidirectional_spectrum(wavenumber_rad_m, wind_speed_m_s, inverse_wave_age)[source]¶

Omnidirectional sea-surface elevation spectrum S(k) (Elfouhaily et al., 1997).

Unified long- plus short-wave wind-wave spectrum. The omnidirectional curvature (saturation) spectrum is B(k) = B_low(k) + B_high(k); this returns S(k) = B(k) / k^3. Unlike the Cox-Munk slope variances (which integrate the whole wave field), this resolves the spectral density at a single wavenumber – the quantity Bragg backscatter needs at the resonant wavenumber k_Bragg = 2 k sin(theta).

Reference: Elfouhaily, Chapron, Katsaros, Vandemark, “A unified directional spectrum for long and short wind-driven waves”, J. Geophys. Res. 102(C7), 15781-15796, 1997.

Parameters:

  • wavenumber_rad_m (scalar or array) – Spatial wavenumber k = 2 pi / wavelength [rad/m] (> 0).

  • wind_speed_m_s (scalar) – Wind speed at 10 m reference height U10 [m/s] (> 0).

  • inverse_wave_age (scalar) – Inverse wave age Omega_c [-] (0.84 fully developed, up to about 5 for young seas).

Returns:

Omnidirectional elevation spectrum S(k) [m^3].

Return type:

scalar or array

functions.ocean_physics.bragg_scattering_coefficients(theta_inc_rad, eps_r)[source]¶

First-order small-perturbation (Bragg) scattering coefficients for H and V polarisation.

These are the polarisation amplitudes in the SPM/Bragg backscatter cross-section sigma0_pp ~ k^4 cos^4(theta) |g_pp|^2 W(2 k sin theta). They are NOT the Fresnel reflection coefficients: they reduce to a common value at normal incidence (g_HH(0) = g_VV(0) = (eps - 1) / (1 + sqrt(eps))^2), and |g_VV| exceeds |g_HH| at oblique incidence for a high-permittivity surface such as seawater.

Reference: Valenzuela (1978); Ulaby, Moore and Fung, “Microwave Remote Sensing” Vol. II.

Parameters:

  • theta_inc_rad (scalar or array) – Incidence angle from the surface normal [rad].

  • eps_r (complex) – Relative permittivity of seawater.

Returns:

(g_hh, g_vv) complex Bragg scattering coefficients for horizontal and vertical polarisation.

Return type:

tuple

functions.ocean_physics.bragg_backscatter_nrcs(theta_inc_rad, wavelength_m, eps_r, wind_speed_m_s, inverse_wave_age)[source]¶

First-order Bragg (small-perturbation) ocean backscatter NRCS for circular polarisation.

Resonant scattering from the wind-driven ripple at the Bragg wavenumber k_B = 2 k sin(theta), with k = 2 pi / wavelength. This is the return the geometric-optics glistening model misses at oblique incidence (no facets tilted enough to retroreflect) and that dominates ocean backscatter beyond about 20 deg incidence. The cross-section is sigma0_pp = 8 pi k^4 cos^4(theta) |g_pp|^2 W_iso(k_B) with the isotropic 2-D spectrum W_iso(K) = S(K) / (2 pi K) from the Elfouhaily S(k), and the circular amplitudes g_RL = (g_HH + g_VV) / 2 (RHCP to LHCP, handedness flipped) and g_RR = (g_HH - g_VV) / 2 (RHCP to RHCP, preserved). The 8-pi prefactor is the textbook SPM constant; with the Elfouhaily normalisation it places sigma0_RL in a broad L-band plausibility envelope without a fitted scale. This is not a polarisation-matched measurement validation. SPM validity holds for moderate incidence (about 10 to 70 deg); near nadir k_B -> 0, the Bragg return vanishes and the geometric-optics term owns the geometry, so this returns 0 there.

Reference: Valenzuela (1978); Ulaby, Moore and Fung, “Microwave Remote Sensing” Vol. II.

Parameters:

  • theta_inc_rad (scalar or array) – Incidence angle from the surface normal [rad].

  • wavelength_m (float) – Radar wavelength [m].

  • eps_r (complex) – Seawater relative permittivity.

  • wind_speed_m_s (scalar) – Wind speed at 10 m [m/s].

  • inverse_wave_age (scalar) – Inverse wave age Omega_c [-].

Returns:

(sigma0_RL, sigma0_RR) cross-pol and co-pol NRCS [dimensionless]; 0 at or below nadir.

Return type:

tuple

functions.ocean_physics.large_scale_slope_variances(wavelength_m, wind_speed_m_s, inverse_wave_age)[source]¶

Mean-square slope of the large-scale (tilting) waves below k_radar / 3, in the wind frame.

Integrates the Elfouhaily slope spectrum k^2 S(k) up to the two-scale division wavenumber for the total large-scale slope variance, then splits it by the Cox-Munk upwind/crosswind anisotropy ratio.

Parameters:

  • wavelength_m (float) – Radar wavelength [m].

  • wind_speed_m_s (scalar) – Wind speed at 10 m [m/s].

  • inverse_wave_age (scalar) – Inverse wave age Omega_c [-].

Returns:

(s_u_L_sq, s_c_L_sq) large-scale upwind / crosswind slope variances [dimensionless].

Return type:

tuple

functions.ocean_physics.two_scale_backscatter_nrcs(theta_inc_rad, azimuth_rad, wavelength_m, eps_r, wind_speed_m_s, inverse_wave_age)[source]¶

Two-scale (tilt-modulated) ocean backscatter NRCS for circular polarisation.

Averages the first-order Bragg NRCS over the large-scale facet-slope distribution: each tilting facet presents a local incidence angle theta_local, the Bragg return is evaluated there, and the result is averaged over the anisotropic large-scale slope PDF. This adds the tilt-modulation lift at low incidence and the upwind/crosswind asymmetry that first-order Bragg misses, and reduces to bragg_backscatter_nrcs as the large-scale slope -> 0. The out-of-plane tilt-induced polarisation rotation is not yet included (a smaller correction; documented as a further refinement).

Parameters:

  • theta_inc_rad (scalar or array) – Incidence angle from the (mean) surface normal [rad].

  • azimuth_rad (scalar or array) – Radar look azimuth relative to the upwind axis [rad].

  • wavelength_m (float) – Radar wavelength [m].

  • eps_r (complex) – Seawater relative permittivity.

  • wind_speed_m_s (scalar) – Sea-state inputs (as in bragg_backscatter_nrcs()).

  • inverse_wave_age (scalar) – Sea-state inputs (as in bragg_backscatter_nrcs()).

Returns:

(sigma0_RL, sigma0_RR) tilt-averaged cross-pol and co-pol NRCS.

Return type:

tuple

Module Assumptions and Limitations¶

  • Valid sea-state range. Klein-Swift is fit for roughly -2 to 30 degC and 0 to 40 PSU; Cox-Munk is for clean (slick-free) seas; Bragg holds for moderate incidence (about 10 to 70 deg).

  • Near-nadir Bragg divergence. First-order Bragg grows without bound toward nadir (\(\sigma^0 \sim B/(4\sin^4\theta)\) as the resonant wavenumber slides into the energetic long-wave spectrum), and the two-scale tilt average leaks that growth through mirror-ward-tilted facets well above nadir. The consuming ocean target therefore gates the Bragg term to incidence at or above 20 deg (divergence protection); below that the quasi-specular geometric-optics term owns the return.

  • First-order Bragg. The small-ripple theory is first order; the two-scale model adds the tilt average but still leaves out the out-of-plane polarisation rotation (a smaller correction, noted as future work).

  • Numerical two-scale quadrature. The large-scale slope average uses a fixed 15 by 15 grid over \(\pm3\) standard deviations and renormalises visible facets. Convergence for extreme wind or grazing incidence is not adaptively controlled.

  • Circular vs linear references. The model gives circular-polarisation results, while many published L-band measurements are linear (V/H); comparisons are envelope-and-trend, not exact dB matches.

  • Sign convention. The imaginary part of the permittivity is negative here (exp(+j omega t)); losses add on that side.

Validation and Tests¶

tests/test_ocean_physics.py provides implementation verification at several levels:

Test group

What it checks

TestSeawaterPermittivity

An L-band seawater value lies in a broad expected range; the high-frequency limit tends to 4.9.

TestFresnelCoefficients / TestCircularPolReflectivities

Closed-form limits at normal incidence and grazing; reflectivity never exceeds 1 (no energy gain).

TestCoxMunkSlopeVariances / TestCoxMunkSlopePdf

Slope variance grows with wind; the slope PDF integrates to 1.

TestElfouhailySpectrum

Spectrum positivity, shape and wind/wave-age trends are regression-checked.

TestBraggScatteringCoefficients / TestBraggBackscatterNrcs

Bragg amplitude identities hold at nadir; a representative L-band value is constrained to a broad plausibility interval and angular trends are checked.

TestLargeScaleSlopeVariances / TestTwoScaleBackscatterNrcs

The tilt average lifts the low-incidence return, adds upwind/crosswind anisotropy, and preserves scalar/array consistency at intermediate azimuth.

The distinction matters: these tests can expose coding and unit errors, but an absolute NRCS claim still requires comparison with polarisation-matched measurements under known wind, wave-age and incidence conditions.

User Guide¶

These are internal physics helpers; you do not call them directly from a run. They are driven by the [OCEAN] sea-state settings (wind, temperature, salinity, wave age) through OceanTarget. See that page for the configuration keys.

References¶

  • Klein, L. & Swift, C., “An improved model for the dielectric constant of sea water at microwave frequencies”, IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag. 25(1), 1977.

  • Cox, C. & Munk, W., “Measurement of the roughness of the sea surface from photographs of the sun’s glitter”, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 44(11), 1954.

  • Elfouhaily, T. et al., “A unified directional spectrum for long and short wind-driven waves”, JGR 102(C7), 1997.

  • Valenzuela, G., “Theories for the interaction of electromagnetic and oceanic waves – a review”, Boundary-Layer Meteorol. 13, 1978.
